flawed_step: The 'only if' half of the claim (stated at lines 0006-0007 and deferred at line 0016): the text proves only Theorem 1 (acyclic => unique reduction, lines 0017-0033) and stops mid-sentence at line 0033 without ever establishing 'unique transitive reduction => acyclic'. That missing direction is not merely unproved, it is false.
counterexample:
Take the 2-cycle. V = {a, b}, E = {(a,b), (b,a)}. G is cyclic.

Transitive closure (using the proof's own convention, line 0010, that a directed path has positive length): the positive-length paths are a->b, b->a, a->b->a, b->a->b, so E_T = {(a,b), (b,a), (a,a), (b,b)}.

Minimum-edge H = (V, F) with H_T = G_T: F must force (a,b) in H_T, i.e. a directed path a ~> b in H. Take a shortest such path; a shortest path repeats no vertex, and on two vertices the only vertex-distinct path from a to b is the single edge (a,b) (a loop (a,a) or (b,b) can never shorten or start such a path). Hence (a,b) in F, and symmetrically (b,a) in F. So |F| >= 2. Conversely F = {(a,b), (b,a)} already has closure exactly {(a,b),(b,a),(a,a),(b,b)} = E_T. Therefore the minimum is 2 edges and every minimum F contains both (a,b) and (b,a), so F = {(a,b),(b,a)} is forced: the transitive reduction is UNIQUE, namely G itself.

So G is cyclic yet has a unique transitive reduction, refuting 'unique => acyclic'. (The same holds if one instead bars self-loops from G_T: then G_T = {(a,b),(b,a)} and the unique minimum reduction is again G.) The witness is minimal in the sense that the intended converse only starts working at cycle length >= 3: for the 3-cycle a->b->c->a, G_T is complete-with-loops and both a->b->c->a and a->c->b->a are 3-edge reductions, which is presumably the argument the truncated page 2 was heading toward; it does not cover the 2-cycle.
reasoning_summary: Verified the visible steps in order. Lines 0009-0015 (setup and definitions) are fine. Lines 0018-0022: for a DAG, reachability by positive-length paths is a strict partial order (the proof writes it as a partial order with the reflexive symbol, a harmless abuse since it immediately uses the strict relation). Lines 0022-0026: cover relation and Hasse diagram H are correctly defined. Lines 0027-0029: H_T = G_T is a genuine standard fact for finite posets. Lines 0030-0033: the deletion argument is correct as far as it goes -- with no parallel edges, removing the cover edge (u,v) leaves only paths of length >= 2, whose intermediate vertex w would give u < w < v, contradicting that (u,v) is a cover. (Note this only establishes edge-minimality of H, not yet minimum cardinality or uniqueness among all graphs; the standard upgrade -- every H' with H'_T = G_T must contain each cover edge -- was presumably on the truncated page.) So no individual visible step fails. The proof nevertheless fails as a proof of the stated result: it never reaches the 'only if' direction, and that direction is false, so no continuation could have repaired it. Witness: the 2-cycle is cyclic but has a unique transitive reduction (itself), verified above. Verdict INVALID with the counterexample attached to the unproved-and-unprovable half of the biconditional.
